_readme: WORKED EXAMPLE of a variant config. It holds ONLY what it changes.
Use it as:  run = dapt_lib.open_run(CFG_PATH, overrides='ctx4096.json')
(a bare name also resolves next to base.json)
Deep-merge semantics: dicts merge key-by-key; everything else -- including
ARRAYS -- is replaced wholesale. So a variant that changes the grid must
restate the whole `grid` array. That is why the grid is repeated below.
HOW TO CHANGE CONTEXT: set an ARM's max_length. Do NOT touch budget.seq_len.
seq_len is the reference length the token budget is defined at (45.6M
tokens/arm = steps x effective_batch x seq_len); raising it would silently
double the token budget instead of changing context. check_config() warns
if seq_len and the baseline's own max_length ever diverge.
_variant_why: 4096 context is a DEPLOYMENT choice, not an ablation: it answers 'does the
arm ranking survive at the context I will actually serve at?'
B4k sees the same 45.6M tokens as B (tokens/arm is held constant), so it
gets half the steps: 696 instead of 1392. Its wall-clock estimate is
OPTIMISTIC -- sec_per_step was measured at 2048, and per-step cost scales
roughly with sequence length. If B4k matters, re-probe at 4096 and set
sec_per_step from that measurement before trusting its hours.
This variant drops LR3e4 and ADONLY to stay inside the 45 h ceiling.
